android-settings.add.added.one: 1 person joins on first sign-in to {app}.
android-settings.add.added.other: {n} people join on first sign-in to {app}.

android-settings.add.note: Added directly to “{name}”, no accepting needed. People who've used {app} join now; others join when they first sign in with this email.
android-settings.add.title: Add members
android-settings.appearance.title: Appearance
android-settings.changelog.title: Changelog
android-settings.connect.deleteText: Disconnects from Slack. Delete the app in Slack yourself.

android-settings.connect.deleteTextSessi.one: Disconnects from Slack. Its chat is kept but gets no new messages. Delete the app in Slack yourself.
android-settings.connect.deleteTextSessi.other: Disconnects from Slack. Its {n} chats are kept but get no new messages. Delete the app in Slack yourself.

android-settings.connect.everyMessage: Gets every message it can see.
android-settings.connect.noSession: No chat yet; the next message starts one.
android-settings.connect.noSessions: No chats yet. @{name} in Slack to start one.
android-settings.connect.ownerNote: The owner sees this connect under “Mine”.
android-settings.connect.runtime: Runs on {runtime}, which can't be changed; for another runtime, add a new connect. Ongoing chats keep their settings.
android-settings.connect.slackAppNote: Changes go straight to the Slack app
android-settings.connects.note: A connect is where people reach {app}, such as a Slack app. Each connect lives on a station and is bound to a model.
android-settings.connects.title: Connects
android-settings.env.note: Variables the runtime starts with, to reach your model service. {route} in a value becomes the chat's route ID.
android-settings.env.title: Environment
android-settings.files.clearAll.text: Deletes the {size} of chat history and files kept on this phone; they download again when opened.
android-settings.files.clearAll.title: Clear all?
android-settings.files.clearChat.text: Deletes the {size} kept on this phone; it downloads again when opened.
android-settings.files.data.text: Sign-in, chat lists, settings; not deletable
android-settings.files.messages.clear: Deletes this chat's messages kept on this phone; they are read again from the station when it is opened.
android-settings.files.messages.text: Read again from the station when opened
android-settings.files.note: Chat history and files opened on this phone are kept here so they show again without downloading. Deleting them only affects this phone, not the station.
android-settings.files.temporary.text: Deletes temporary files left by marking images and the like.
android-settings.files.title: Storage on this phone
android-settings.files.web.text: Deletes what previewed pages kept; they load again when opened.
android-settings.flow.appToken: On the Socket Mode page, generate an App-Level Token and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes preset).
android-settings.flow.installManual: App created. Install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) from the OAuth page.
android-settings.flow.installOauth: App created. Install it to the workspace: tap “Allow” in Slack and the bot token goes to the station.
android-settings.flow.manual: Set up manually, no config token
android-settings.flow.manual1: Create a Slack app from {app}'s manifest.
android-settings.flow.manual2: On its Socket Mode page, generate an App-Level Token (scopes preset).
android-settings.flow.manual3: On the Install App page, install to the workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
android-settings.flow.manualInSlack: Set up in Slack manually, no config token
android-settings.flow.noModels: No models enabled in this station's profiles. Enable some under Profile on the station page.
android-settings.flow.noProfileNote: Connects run models through a profile. Add one first.
android-settings.flow.permsNote: Permissions default to all on; change them later under the connect's “Slack app”.
android-settings.flow.removeTokenText: {app} stops using it to build and edit apps in this Slack workspace. Existing apps and connects aren't affected; you can add it again later.
android-settings.flow.title: Add connect
android-settings.flow.tokenNote: With a Slack config token, {app} creates the app for you: set its name, icon and permissions here instead of in Slack's admin pages. Only you can use the token.
android-settings.flow.whichTeam: Which Slack workspace's config token to use.
android-settings.login.codexNote: On the OpenAI page, sign in with the ChatGPT account {app} should use, then paste the code. This continues on its own. If device code sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings first.
android-settings.login.manual: Or sign in by hand on that machine
android-settings.login.note: Sign-in runs on the machine running {app}; you just authorize it in the browser.
android-settings.login.openPageRest: , sign in with the Claude account {app} should use, and agree.
android-settings.login.signedIn: Signed in. Sign in again to switch accounts.
android-settings.login.step2: 2. After you agree, copy the code shown:
android-settings.machine.added: Profile added with this machine's login
android-settings.machine.title: Already signed in here
android-settings.me.title: Account
android-settings.members.moveOutText: They lose access to this workspace's stations. You can invite them again later.
android-settings.members.title: Members
android-settings.mode.back: Switching back to single chat later resumes the original one.
android-settings.mode.keepSession: Resumes the single chat it was bound to before.
android-settings.mode.mention: From now on only @-mentioned threads go into chats; replies in threads already in still arrive.
android-settings.mode.mentionOff: Gets every message it can see in its channels.
android-settings.mode.mentionOn: Replies in an @-mentioned thread don't need another @.
android-settings.mode.newSession: The next message starts a new single chat, or pick an existing chat after switching.
android-settings.mode.noMention: No @ needed: every message in every channel and DM it can see goes to the agent. Uses noticeably more.
android-settings.mode.oldThreads: Threads from the single chat need a new @ to continue, which opens a new chat without the earlier context.

android-settings.mode.running.one: 1 chat is running; it finishes its current turn.
android-settings.mode.running.other: {n} chats are running; they finish their current turn.

android-settings.mode.title: Chat mode
android-settings.mode.toMulti: The bound chat gets no new messages. Each thread then opens its own chat when @-mentioned.
android-settings.mode.toSingle: All its messages then go into one chat. Existing per-thread chats get no new messages, even replies in their threads. Their history is kept.
android-settings.models.empty: Once the profile is checked, its models are listed here. Tick the ones to use.
android-settings.models.note: Only ticked models show up in chats and connects.
android-settings.notify.on: Done, needs you, failed, new messages
android-settings.notify.title: Notifications
android-settings.profile.background: Background commands when a message arrives
android-settings.profile.backgroundOff: New messages wait until the running command or subagent finishes.
android-settings.profile.backgroundOn: Commands and subagents continue in the background; the agent reads the message at once.
android-settings.profile.deleteText: Removes it from {app} only; its config directory and login stay. Sessions running on it move to another Profile, or stop when there is none.
android-settings.profile.disableText: {app} stops using the {runtime} login on this machine. The login itself stays, and you can use it again later. Sessions running on it move to another Profile, or stop when there is none.
android-settings.profile.fastNote: For chats on Plan default; Fast uses more allowance or credits
android-settings.profile.machineNote: To switch accounts, sign in again or sign out, use {runtime} on this machine; this profile follows. To stop using it, turn it off (top-right menu).
android-settings.profile.noUsers: No connects use this profile yet.
android-settings.profile.offline: {name} is offline; available once it reconnects
android-settings.profile.subscriptionNot: Sign-in runs on the machine running {app}; you just authorize it in the browser. The profile is added once sign-in succeeds.
android-settings.profiles.note: Accounts agents run models with. Ones that need a look come first; open one to see why and how to fix it.
android-settings.quota.title: Allowance
android-settings.relays.hint: An iroh-relay https address. The web app needs a publicly issued certificate (such as Let's Encrypt); a self-signed one won't do.
android-settings.relays.lead: Stations and members' devices also connect through these relays, besides {app}'s, taking the quickest.
android-settings.relays.title: Relays
android-settings.run.noModels: No models enabled in {runtime} profiles. Enable some under Profile on the station page.
android-settings.run.note: New chats use the new settings; ongoing ones keep theirs.
android-settings.run.title: Model
android-settings.session.note: Messages to “{name}” now go into the chosen chat. The previous chat is kept but gets no new messages from this connect.
android-settings.session.title: Choose chat
android-settings.signIn.many: Sign in with several accounts; switch workspaces any time.
android-settings.signIn.note: After sign-in, every station and chat in your workspaces shows up here.
android-settings.signIn.title: Keep your agents working
android-settings.slack.accessToken: That's the Access Token. Use the Refresh Token below it (xoxe-1-…).
android-settings.slack.approveNote: Permissions changed; approve them in Slack to take effect.
android-settings.slack.group.base.note: Get messages when @-mentioned; read and reply in its channels, DMs and group DMs. Required.
android-settings.slack.group.canvases.no: Create, edit and read canvases, e.g. write a plan or report as a canvas in a channel.
android-settings.slack.group.channels.no: Create channels, invite people, see joins and new channels.
android-settings.slack.group.connect.not: See, send and accept invites to channels shared with other companies.
android-settings.slack.group.customize.n: Change display name and icon per message.
android-settings.slack.group.dm.note: Open DMs with one or more people.
android-settings.slack.group.extras.note: Unfurl links, set reminders, read DND and call status.
android-settings.slack.group.files.note: Read attachments; upload screenshots, logs and other files.
android-settings.slack.group.lists.note: Create, edit and read Slack Lists, e.g. keep a task list.
android-settings.slack.group.more.note: Set its presence, read message metadata and workspace settings, embed video links, answer slash commands.
android-settings.slack.group.people.note: Read emails, profiles, user groups, workspace info and custom emoji.
android-settings.slack.group.public.note: Reply in public channels without an invite.
android-settings.slack.group.reactions.n: Mark progress with emoji, pin messages, manage bookmarks.
android-settings.slack.group.search.note: Search public messages and files, find people by name, look up context to answer.
android-settings.slack.group.topics.note: Set topics and purposes of channels and DMs; invite people to channels.
Create user groups, edit members, start and update calls.
android-settings.slack.iconNote: Pick one below, or upload an image.
android-settings.slack.name: Name
android-settings.slack.needToken: To edit the app here, add your app config token for this Slack workspace. Only you can use it; others on this station can't see it.
android-settings.slack.noApp: Can't find this connect's Slack app ({error}). Switch to a valid token, then come back.
android-settings.slack.notConnected: Edit its app here once it's connected to Slack.
android-settings.slack.refreshToken: The Refresh Token starts with xoxe-1-.
android-settings.slack.step1: Open api.slack.com/apps and sign in to the Slack workspace the bot will join.
android-settings.slack.step2: Scroll to “Your App Configuration Tokens” at the bottom, tap Generate Token and pick this workspace.
android-settings.slack.step3: Paste the Refresh Token (xoxe-1-…) below. {app} renews it from then on.
android-settings.slack.updatedApprove: Updated; approve the new permissions in Slack
android-settings.station.addNote: A station is a machine running {app}. Name it, then run the generated command in its terminal: it installs {app} and joins.
android-settings.station.firstNote: Agents work on your machines. Start by adding a Mac or Linux machine.
android-settings.station.joined: “{name}” joined. You can open it now.
android-settings.station.name: Name
android-settings.station.removeText: It disconnects from {app} cloud and members can't reach it from here. {app} and data on the machine stay; you can add it again later.
android-settings.station.runNote: Works on macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux, including machines with {app} already. It installs {app}, joins this workspace and keeps running in the background. Then add profiles on its station page.
android-settings.station.wait: No stations yet. An admin needs to add one.
android-settings.station.waiting: Waiting for the machine… Continues once the command runs · Valid for 1 hour
android-settings.stations.offline: Offline: open {app} on this machine to reconnect
android-settings.stations.silent: Hasn't reached {app} in a long time
android-settings.title: Settings
android-settings.tokens.note: Change one or both; a blank one keeps the saved value.
android-settings.waiting.removeText: Removes it from {app} only; the app stays in Slack. Delete it from the app's settings in Slack if you no longer need it.

android-settings.workspace.deleteText.one: All members lose access, and 1 station disconnects from {app} cloud (data on the station stays).
android-settings.workspace.deleteText.other: All members lose access, and {n} stations disconnect from {app} cloud (data on them stays).

android-settings.workspace.leaveText: You'll lose access to its stations and need a new invite to return.
android-settings.workspace.name: Workspace name
